question: What is the primary role of community mobilisation in primary health care?

options.A: Empowering locals to drive health actions

explanation: Community mobilisation focuses on building local capacity so people can take charge of their own health needs. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why is a top-down medical approach discouraged in community mobilisation?

options.A: It requires too many doctors in rural clinics
options.B: It relies entirely on international donor funds
options.C: It ignores local priorities and participation
options.D: It is too expensive for local health budgets

explanation: True mobilisation requires active community involvement rather than imposing solutions without local input. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h1)

question: What is a main objective of resource mobilisation in health programs?

options.C: Reducing the salaries of health workers

explanation: Resource mobilisation looks inward to utilise available local assets and human capital for sustainability. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h2)

question: Why is promoting community ownership a vital objective?

options.A: It removes the need for trained nurses
options.B: It ensures projects survive after partners leave
options.C: It eliminates all local health risks instantly
options.D: It prevents the government from paying taxes

explanation: When a community owns a project, they maintain it independently once external support ends. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h2)

question: Which principle ensures that vulnerable groups participate in health decisions?
explanation: Equity and inclusion mean every segment of the population has an equal opportunity to contribute and benefit. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why must health workers respect cultural relevance during mobilisation?

options.A: To gain acceptance and build community trust
options.B: To avoid learning new local dialects
options.D: To reduce the duration of health talks

explanation: Aligning health messages with local culture reduces resistance and fosters genuine engagement. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h3)

question: Who are considered key gatekeepers in community mobilisation?
explanation: Traditional and religious leaders hold significant social influence over community attitudes and behaviors. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h4)

question: How do influential stakeholders affect health intervention outcomes?

options.B: They sway public opinion and encourage participation
options.C: They replace community health nurses entirely
options.D: They provide all the funding for infrastructure

explanation: Their endorsement builds immediate credibility and trust for health programs among local residents. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the very first step in the community mobilisation process?
explanation: Before acting, workers must enter the community properly and assess what problems actually exist. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why is holding town hall meetings important during the sensitisation phase?

options.B: To distribute financial loans to families
options.C: To select political candidates for office
options.D: To discuss findings and agree on priorities

explanation: Town hall meetings provide a platform for open dialogue and consensus on what needs fixing first. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h5)

question: What causes project fatigue in many rural communities?
explanation: Communities grow weary and skeptical when previous projects start and are later abandoned without completion. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h6)

question: How should a nurse handle cultural myths that hinder health campaigns?

options.A: By halting all health activities permanently
options.B: By threatening legal action against elders
options.C: Through consistent dialogue and local champions
options.D: By ignoring the community until they comply

explanation: Patient communication and trusted local figures are effective tools for dispelling harmful myths. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h6)

question: What does monitoring a mobilisation effort primarily involve?
explanation: Monitoring is an ongoing process that keeps track of day-to-day implementation and progress. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h7)

question: Why is participatory evaluation involving community members encouraged?

options.A: It ensures shared accountability and learning
options.B: It reduces the workload of local nurses
options.D: It eliminates the need for written reports

explanation: Involving locals in evaluation helps them see results firsthand and take ownership of lessons learned. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h7)
